editorNote: Two of today's items are about measuring models rather than shipping them: Anthropic's read on an open-weight model's cyber skills and a hobbyist's attempt to catch a quiet regression. Bain's revenue arithmetic and Delhi's grid round out a day of numbers over announcements.

stories.headline: Anthropic: Zhipu's open-weight GLM-5.3 can build working exploits, and its safeguards are easy to bypass
stories.summary: Anthropic reports GLM-5.3 produced working exploits in 50 of 410 ExploitBench attempts (12%) and 4% on its internal binary-exploitation test, where earlier models scored near zero. The model never refused outright, engaged 64% of the time with a false cover story and 100% with an abliterated version.
stories.whyItMatters: Anthropic argues cyber capability comparable to its restricted Mythos Preview is now available with weaker safeguards, and calls for government testing and wider defender access.

sourceLinks.title: GLM-5.3 and the spread of advanced cyber capabilities (Anthropic)

stories.headline: Bain: AI needs about $6 trillion in annual revenue by 2031 to justify the data-centre build-out
stories.summary: A Bain & Company report says AI infrastructure spending will reach $1.5 trillion a year by 2031, requiring $6 trillion in annual revenue, of which $4.2 trillion would come from new products and $1–1.4 trillion from enterprise productivity. It says data-centre size and cost double every 12–16 months; Meta's Ohio site goes from 600MW and $24 billion in 2025 to a projected 9GW and $200 billion in 2030.
stories.whyItMatters: It is a consultancy's estimate, but it puts a number on how much revenue the current spending pace implies.

sourceLinks.title: AI industry needs to earn $6 trillion by 2031 to justify data centres (The National)

stories.headline: Livenerf sets out to catch Opus 5.5 getting quietly worse after launch, and can't yet tell it from Opus 5
stories.summary: The open repo runs about 80 borderline questions from GPQA Diamond, MMLU-Pro and competition math daily against Opus 5.5, with a parallel Opus 5 as a control. It has logged 6 of 30 baseline days with no missed runs and no flagged change; its own validation could not distinguish Opus 5 from Opus 5.5 at 99% confidence.
stories.whyItMatters: Results are not expected until after day 20, and the author says the design can detect roughly a 7.5-point accuracy shift per 10-day window.

sourceLinks.title: livenerf: Has Opus 5.5 been nerfed yet? (GitHub)

stories.headline: Delhi cut electricity losses from over 50% to 5–6% while peak demand tripled
stories.summary: IEEE Spectrum credits the drop since 2002 to privatised distribution, digital and then smart meters, SCADA monitoring, capacitor banks and better cables, AI-based anomaly detection, and hiring women in low-income areas as bill collectors. Grid reliability rose from about 70% to over 99.9%.
stories.whyItMatters: The loss rate is now comparable to France and Belgium, and the mix of technical, billing and social fixes is the part other utilities can copy.

sourceLinks.title: How Delhi cut electricity loss from 50 to 5 percent (IEEE Spectrum)
